## devonthink
CRITICAL — Database package safety: DEVONthink databases are stored as packages (.dtBase2) or sparse images (.dtSparse, .dtArchive). Never modify, rename, move, or delete files inside a database package directly via the filesystem. All record and content operations must go through this MCP server or, as a fallback, via AppleScript. Direct filesystem manipulation will corrupt the database and cause irreversible data loss.

Batch operations: Use the uuids array parameter instead of sequential single-record calls for tag, update, move, trash, duplicate, replicate, and export operations. Batch mode is faster, reduces round trips, and returns a summary with succeeded/failed counts.

Avoiding duplicates: Use lookup_records (by name, URL, path, filename, or comment) before create_record to check whether a record already exists.

Content editing: Prefer update_record_content with mode append or insert over replace for large documents. Replace mode requires sending the entire new content and risks accidental data loss if the content is incomplete.

Group hierarchies: Use create_group_path to create nested group structures in a single call (like mkdir -p) rather than sequential create_record calls.

AI-powered tools: classify_record and find_similar_records use DEVONthink's built-in AI algorithms and proprietary training data — they provide organizational suggestions that complement, not duplicate, your own capabilities.

Record enrichment: resolve_doi_metadata and resolve_book_metadata can enrich existing records with bibliographic metadata by passing the record's uuid — there is no need to create a new record.

AI exclusion: Records marked as excluded from AI access (excludeFromChat) are protected in two ways. (1) Input protection: any tool that receives such a record's UUID as an argument refuses to operate on it and returns an error. 1	# Spending Report Design
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-07-09
4	**Status:** ✅ Built — table + chart views, cell drill-down, and hierarchy
5	editing (assign categories to groups, re-parent groups) are all shipped and live.
6	Remaining work is the [Deferred](#deferred-later-slices) slices (historical-year
7	upload / year-over-year, period selection, tier CRUD, export).
8	
9	## Overview
10	
11	A top-level **Spending** report that rolls up Expenses by **Importance →
12	Grouping → Category** across the months of a year. It replaces the Excel pivot
13	table the family currently maintains by hand. ("Spending Report" is the working
14	term; pin the final ubiquitous-language name in `domain-model.md` when built.)
15	
16	Built ✅: the **table view** (v1), the **chart view** (an accordion magnitude bar
17	chart), **cell drill-down** into the Expenses view, and **hierarchy editing**
18	(assign categories to groups, re-parent groups, assign-on-create) — see
19	[Implementation status](#implementation-status),
20	[Spending Chart](#spending-chart-graphical-presentation--built-),
21	[Drill-down](#drill-from-a-table-cell-into-the-expenses-view--built-), and
22	[Editable hierarchy](#editable-hierarchy--assign--re-parent--built-). Still
23	deferred: selectable periods, year-over-year comparison, historical-year upload,
24	tier CRUD, and export (see [Deferred](#deferred-later-slices)).
25	
26	## Data model (new)
27	
28	The category hierarchy today is flat: `categories (family_id, name, color)`.
29	There is no Grouping or Importance layer. v1 adds two tiers as real,
30	family-scoped tables so they are first-class and become editable later.
31	
32	- `importance_areas (id, family_id, name, sort_order)` — e.g. Essential
33	  (sort_order 1), Priorities (2), Other (3). The numeric prefix in the sample
34	  (`1. Essential`) becomes `sort_order`, not part of the name.
35	- `category_groups (id, family_id, name, importance_area_id)` — **Importance
36	  attaches to the Grouping**, not to individual categories. Matches the sample
37	  (all of Transportation is Essential) and makes the roll-up a clean two-hop
38	  join. If a future need arises for two categories in one group to have
39	  different importances, revisit — no counterexample in the current sample.
40	- `categories` gains `group_id → category_groups`. A Category belongs to a
41	  Group; the Group carries the Importance.
42	
43	**Seeding.** Derive default Importance areas and Groupings from
44	`docs/SampleHierachy.txt` (cleaned). Map the existing default categories into
45	Groups by name. Near-duplicate categories in the sample (`Car - Insurance` vs
46	`Car insurance`, `Gas` vs `Car - Gas`, `Parking` vs `Car - Parking`) are **not
47	auto-merged** — recognizable names are mapped, the rest fall to Uncategorized.
48	New families are seeded via the same path as `createDefaultCategories`, so any
49	future family gets a working report out of the box.
50	
51	## Report content
52	
53	- **Source:** receipts/Expenses (the app's source of truth for spending), **not**
54	  bank transactions. Bucketed by `transaction_date` (purchase date, not upload
55	  date).
56	- **Currency:** normalized to the family's display currency —
57	  `total_amount × (exchange_rate_to_cad ?? 1)`. CAD for now; the assumption is
58	  isolated so multi-currency drops in later.
59	- **Columns:** January → the last month that has any expense (left edge stays at
60	  January for a stable calendar grid). Interior/empty cells render blank, not
61	  `$0.00`. Final column is labelled **"Year to Date."**
62	- **Rows:** four row types — category detail, **Grouping subtotal**,
63	  **Importance subtotal**, and a final **Grand Total**. Importance ordered by
64	  `sort_order` (Essential → Priorities → Other); Groupings alphabetical within an
65	  Importance; Categories alphabetical within a Grouping. **Zero-activity rows are
66	  suppressed** (a category/group with no spend in the visible window is hidden).
67	- **Uncategorized:** rendered as its own section at the bottom, outside the real
68	  Importance/Grouping subtotals. It **is included in the Grand Total** (and any
69	  month-column totals), so the bottom-right number ties out to the family's
70	  actual total spend. The gap between the three Importance subtotals and the
71	  Grand Total is the deliberate nudge to go categorize.
72	- **Null amounts:** counted as `$0`. No new flag — the receipts and expenses
73	  pages already badge these (`⚠ Amount not read`). At most a small "N receipts
74	  missing an amount" footnote deep-linking to that existing filtered view.
75	
76	## Architecture
77	
78	- **Client-side pure aggregation.** A tested pure function
79	  `buildSpendingReport(expenses, hierarchy, year) → grid`, in the style of the
80	  CSV parsers and date utilities. The small hierarchy tables and the year's
81	  expenses are fetched separately and joined in TypeScript — the existing
82	  expense query is not widened. A family's yearly receipt count is small, so the
83	  data transfer is negligible and the logic stays unit-testable. If volume ever
84	  demands it, swap in a Postgres RPC behind the same function boundary — this
85	  avoids the RLS-fragility minefield the codebase repeatedly warns about.
86	- **Placement:** a new top-level **`/spending`** tab, following the existing
87	  `resolve()` / `filterQuery` nav pattern. May be promoted to the home page
88	  later once proven (currently `/` is "Family Receipts") — a separate change.
89	- **No editing UI in v1.** The hierarchy is hand-maintained (direct SQL) while
90	  the family is a single maintainer. The Uncategorized bucket is the feedback
91	  loop for anything unmapped.
92	
93	## Implementation status ✅
94	
95	v1 is built and running against live data (v0.50). What landed:
96	
97	- **Migration** `supabase/migrations/20260709_spending_hierarchy.sql` — creates
98	  `importance_areas` and `category_groups`, adds `categories.group_id`
99	  (`ON DELETE SET NULL`), family-scoped RLS mirroring `categories_family_access`,
100	  unique-per-family name indexes, and `updated_at` triggers. Ships
101	  `create_default_hierarchy(p_family_id)` (idempotent, `SECURITY DEFINER`): seeds
102	  3 Importance areas + 13 Groupings and maps categories → groups by name (a
103	  superset covering both the current default names and the older spreadsheet
104	  names). Backfills every existing family in a `DO` loop; the app calls it via
105	  RPC for new families.
106	- **Grouping → Importance seed choices.** Each Grouping is collapsed to a single
107	  Importance (the model attaches Importance to the Grouping): **Essential** =
108	  Everyday, Health, Home, Transportation, Income Taxes; **Priorities** = Banking
109	  & Investing, Debt, Fitness, Kids, Rental; **Other** = Discretionary, Gifts,
110	  Travel. Where the source spreadsheet split a Grouping across importances (e.g.
111	  Home's Garden/Household goods were "Other"), it now rolls up under the
112	  Grouping's single Importance. Change with a one-row `UPDATE` on
113	  `category_groups.importance_area_id`.
114	- **Aggregation** `src/lib/utils/spendingReport.ts` — the pure
115	  `buildSpendingReport(expenses, categories, groups, importanceAreas, year)`.
116	  21 unit tests in `spendingReport.spec.ts` (month columns, roll-up/subtotals,
117	  ordering, Uncategorized, refund netting, FX, null amounts, blank-vs-zero cells).
118	  Per-cell `{ amount, count }` drives blank (count 0) vs `0.00` (net-zero but had
119	  activity).
120	- **Types** `src/lib/types/Hierarchy.ts` (`ImportanceArea`, `CategoryGroup`);
121	  `Category` gains `group_id`.
122	- **Service** `CategoryService` gains `getFamilyImportanceAreas`,
123	  `getFamilyGroups`, and `createDefaultHierarchy` (RPC wrapper).
124	- **Page + nav** `src/routes/spending/+page.svelte` + a **Spending** top-level
125	  tab. Self-seeds the hierarchy on first open (mirrors default-categories
126	  lazy-init), then loads hierarchy + the year's expenses and paints the grid.
127	  Year prev/next selector, missing-amount footnote, Importance bands, Grouping
128	  and Importance subtotals, Uncategorized section, Grand Total.
129	- **Rendering details.** Long category names truncate to one line
130	  (`max-w-64 truncate`) with the full name on hover via `title`. The layout gives
131	  `/spending` full window width (`max-w-full`); other pages keep `max-w-5xl`.
132	
133	**Verification:** `npm run check`, `eslint`, and Prettier clean on touched files;
134	full unit suite green (1278 passed / 8 skipped, incl. the 21 new). Production
135	build succeeds. Not yet exercised: a rendered end-to-end pass (no local
136	auth/seed harness) — validated live by the maintainer instead.
137	
138	**Known open item surfaced by live data:** the seed maps by name, so any custom
139	or renamed category lands in Uncategorized until its `group_id` is set by hand.
140	
141	## Spending Chart (graphical presentation) — built ✅
142	
143	A `Table | Chart` toggle on `/spending` (shared year selector + loaded data)
144	adds a **magnitude bar chart** view (v0.60).
145	
146	> **Design note — why not stacked-by-month.** The first cut stacked 12 month
147	> segments per bar with a sequential ramp. In real data it failed twice: the 12
148	> subtle shades read as noise ("the gradient is a mess"), and one dominant
149	> Grouping (a family's ~$33k Home, driven by a one-off $20k renovation) crushed
150	> every other bar's height so small bars were unreadable. Both flaws trace to the
151	> month stack. v0.60 drops it: **solid magnitude bars + value labels**, with the
152	> month/time story deferred to the separate trend chart.
153	
154	- **Form:** one **solid bar per Grouping** = its year-to-date total, **coloured by
155	  Area of Importance** (a validated 3-colour categorical palette: Essential
156	  `#4f46e5`, Priorities `#0d9488`, Other `#d97706`; Uncategorized neutral gray).
157	  Bars ordered by Importance `sort_order` then Grouping name; **Uncategorized**
158	  trails; zero-activity groups suppressed.
159	- **Value label** above every bar (formatted currency), so a tiny bar next to a
160	  dominant one is still readable — the fix for the outlier problem without a
161	  scale hack. Positioned from the bound LayerChart `context` (band x-scale +
162	  linear y-scale).
163	- **Two bracket rows beneath the axis** carry the hierarchy, both positioned from
164	  the bound `context` band x-scale (aligned on resize):
165	  - **Row 1 — Grouping ± toggles.** One keyboard-focusable `<button>` bracket per
166	    Grouping, spanning its bar(s), showing `+ Name` / `− Name`. This is the
167	    expand/collapse control (see interaction) and the Grouping label.
168	  - **Row 2 — Area of Importance**, labelled **once per contiguous run** of
169	    same-Importance bars, in that Importance's colour. Uncategorized has no
170	    Importance bracket (its Grouping bracket names it).
171	- **Interaction: expand in place (accordion), not drill-and-replace.** Clicking a
172	  Grouping's bar **or** its ± bracket expands it into its **Category** bars _in
173	  place_ while its siblings stay visible; **any number of Groupings can be open at
174	  once** (`expandedGroups` is a reactive `SvelteSet`). Expanded Categories keep the
175	  parent Grouping's Importance colour and sit inside the same Importance bracket.
176	  Bars are keyed by a unique id, not name, so same-named Categories across
177	  Groupings don't collide on the band scale.
178	- **Click + hover come from a custom per-bar overlay, not LayerChart.** LayerChart's
179	  own tooltip layer both swallows bar clicks and can't carry a month breakdown, so
180	  `tooltipContext` is disabled and a transparent full-height column is drawn over
181	  each bar (from the band scale). It handles the click (toggle its Grouping) and the
182	  hover, which shows a **tooltip with the bar's name, its per-month totals, and the
183	  grand total** — the monthly detail dropped from the bars themselves. The overlay
184	  columns are `aria-hidden`/non-focusable mouse affordances; the ± brackets remain
185	  the keyboard-accessible controls.
186	- **Long labels don't collide.** When a Grouping expands into many Category bars,
187	  each axis label is truncated to one bar width with an ellipsis (`Meals and Drinks
188	Out` → `Meals…`); the full name is in the hover tooltip. Collapsed Grouping names
189	  live in their ± bracket (truncated there too). The one-line usage hint sits below
190	  the chart.
191	- **Data:** no new aggregation — the pure
192	  `buildSpendingChart(report, expandedGroups)` reshapes the existing
193	  `SpendingReport` into a flat `{ months, bars }` where expanded Groupings
194	  contribute their Category bars in place (unit-tested in `spendingChart.spec.ts`).
195	  The per-bar `monthly` map is retained for the future trend chart / hover detail;
196	  the current view uses only `total`.
197	- **Library:** **LayerChart 2.0.1** (`<BarChart>` with `y="total"` and a `c`
198	  ordinal colour scale by Importance; `bandPadding`, rounded bars). Peer
199	  `svelte@^5`. Its built-in tooltip/click layer (`tooltipContext`) is **disabled**
200	  in favour of the custom overlay above. Colours validated with the dataviz palette
201	  script (CVD ΔE 57.8, contrast ≥ 3:1); identity carried by position + brackets,
202	  not colour alone.
203	- **Verification:** `SpendingChart.svelte.spec.ts` (8 tests) renders it in Chromium
204	  and asserts: a bar per Grouping lays out, the once-only Importance brackets, the
205	  per-bar value labels, expand-in-place (siblings stay), several open at once,
206	  collapse back, **the bar itself (not just the bracket) expands**, and **the hover
207	  tooltip shows name + month totals + grand total**. `spendingChart.spec.ts`
208	  (6 tests) covers the pure accordion model; `spendingReport.spec.ts` (21) the
209	  aggregation.
210	
211	**Chart known limitation:**
212	
213	- **Prior-period overlay** (a line above/below the bar) is **not built** — it
214	  depends on historical-year data, which isn't loaded yet. Deferred with the
215	  upload/YoY thread below. Month-by-month detail currently lives in the Table
216	  view; a dedicated trend chart is the natural home for it.
217	
218	## Drill from a table cell into the Expenses view — built ✅
219	
220	The table's numbers are a jumping-off point (v0.55): clicking a non-blank cell
221	navigates to the **Expenses** view, filtered to exactly the Expenses that
222	produced that number.
223	
224	- **Category detail cell** (category × month) → that **category** in that
225	  **month**. **Category "Year to Date" cell** → that category across the year.
226	- **Subtotal cells** roll the filter up to match what they sum:
227	  - **Grouping subtotal** → every category id in that Grouping (that month/YTD).
228	  - **Importance subtotal** → every category id across the Importance's groups.
229	  - **Grand Total** → the date range alone (no category filter) so it ties out to
230	    all Expenses, **including Uncategorized**.
231	  - **Uncategorized** cells → the `filter=uncategorized` Expenses filter. A
232	    named-but-ungrouped category row instead drills to its own category id
233	    (precise); only the section subtotal and the "(No category)" row use the
234	    coarse `filter=uncategorized` (which by design covers only null-category

# Spending Report Design

**Date:** 2026-07-09
**Status:** ✅ Built — table + chart views, cell drill-down, and hierarchy
editing (assign categories to groups, re-parent groups) are all shipped and live.
Remaining work is the [Deferred](#deferred-later-slices) slices (historical-year
upload / year-over-year, period selection, tier CRUD, export).

## Overview

A top-level **Spending** report that rolls up Expenses by **Importance →
Grouping → Category** across the months of a year. It replaces the Excel pivot
table the family currently maintains by hand. ("Spending Report" is the working
term; pin the final ubiquitous-language name in `domain-model.md` when built.)

Built ✅: the **table view** (v1), the **chart view** (an accordion magnitude bar
chart), **cell drill-down** into the Expenses view, and **hierarchy editing**
(assign categories to groups, re-parent groups, assign-on-create) — see
[Implementation status](#implementation-status),
[Spending Chart](#spending-chart-graphical-presentation--built-),
[Drill-down](#drill-from-a-table-cell-into-the-expenses-view--built-), and
[Editable hierarchy](#editable-hierarchy--assign--re-parent--built-). Still
deferred: selectable periods, year-over-year comparison, historical-year upload,
tier CRUD, and export (see [Deferred](#deferred-later-slices)).

## Data model (new)

The category hierarchy today is flat: `categories (family_id, name, color)`.
There is no Grouping or Importance layer. v1 adds two tiers as real,
family-scoped tables so they are first-class and become editable later.

- `importance_areas (id, family_id, name, sort_order)` — e.g. Essential
  (sort_order 1), Priorities (2), Other (3). The numeric prefix in the sample
  (`1. Essential`) becomes `sort_order`, not part of the name.
- `category_groups (id, family_id, name, importance_area_id)` — **Importance
  attaches to the Grouping**, not to individual categories. Matches the sample
  (all of Transportation is Essential) and makes the roll-up a clean two-hop
  join. If a future need arises for two categories in one group to have
  different importances, revisit — no counterexample in the current sample.
- `categories` gains `group_id → category_groups`. A Category belongs to a
  Group; the Group carries the Importance.

**Seeding.** Derive default Importance areas and Groupings from
`docs/SampleHierachy.txt` (cleaned). Map the existing default categories into
Groups by name. Near-duplicate categories in the sample (`Car - Insurance` vs
`Car insurance`, `Gas` vs `Car - Gas`, `Parking` vs `Car - Parking`) are **not
auto-merged** — recognizable names are mapped, the rest fall to Uncategorized.
New families are seeded via the same path as `createDefaultCategories`, so any
future family gets a working report out of the box.

## Report content

- **Source:** receipts/Expenses (the app's source of truth for spending), **not**
  bank transactions. Bucketed by `transaction_date` (purchase date, not upload
  date).
- **Currency:** normalized to the family's display currency —
  `total_amount × (exchange_rate_to_cad ?? 1)`. CAD for now; the assumption is
  isolated so multi-currency drops in later.
- **Columns:** January → the last month that has any expense (left edge stays at
  January for a stable calendar grid). Interior/empty cells render blank, not
  `$0.00`. Final column is labelled **"Year to Date."**
- **Rows:** four row types — category detail, **Grouping subtotal**,
  **Importance subtotal**, and a final **Grand Total**. Importance ordered by
  `sort_order` (Essential → Priorities → Other); Groupings alphabetical within an
  Importance; Categories alphabetical within a Grouping. **Zero-activity rows are
  suppressed** (a category/group with no spend in the visible window is hidden).
- **Uncategorized:** rendered as its own section at the bottom, outside the real
  Importance/Grouping subtotals. It **is included in the Grand Total** (and any
  month-column totals), so the bottom-right number ties out to the family's
  actual total spend. The gap between the three Importance subtotals and the
  Grand Total is the deliberate nudge to go categorize.
- **Null amounts:** counted as `$0`. No new flag — the receipts and expenses
  pages already badge these (`⚠ Amount not read`). At most a small "N receipts
  missing an amount" footnote deep-linking to that existing filtered view.

## Architecture

- **Client-side pure aggregation.** A tested pure function
  `buildSpendingReport(expenses, hierarchy, year) → grid`, in the style of the
  CSV parsers and date utilities. The small hierarchy tables and the year's
  expenses are fetched separately and joined in TypeScript — the existing
  expense query is not widened. A family's yearly receipt count is small, so the
  data transfer is negligible and the logic stays unit-testable. If volume ever
  demands it, swap in a Postgres RPC behind the same function boundary — this
  avoids the RLS-fragility minefield the codebase repeatedly warns about.
- **Placement:** a new top-level **`/spending`** tab, following the existing
  `resolve()` / `filterQuery` nav pattern. May be promoted to the home page
  later once proven (currently `/` is "Family Receipts") — a separate change.
- **No editing UI in v1.** The hierarchy is hand-maintained (direct SQL) while
  the family is a single maintainer. The Uncategorized bucket is the feedback
  loop for anything unmapped.

v1 is built and running against live data (v0.50). What landed:

- **Migration** `supabase/migrations/20260709_spending_hierarchy.sql` — creates
  `importance_areas` and `category_groups`, adds `categories.group_id`
  (`ON DELETE SET NULL`), family-scoped RLS mirroring `categories_family_access`,
  unique-per-family name indexes, and `updated_at` triggers. Ships
  `create_default_hierarchy(p_family_id)` (idempotent, `SECURITY DEFINER`): seeds
  3 Importance areas + 13 Groupings and maps categories → groups by name (a
  superset covering both the current default names and the older spreadsheet
  names). Backfills every existing family in a `DO` loop; the app calls it via
  RPC for new families.
- **Grouping → Importance seed choices.** Each Grouping is collapsed to a single
  Importance (the model attaches Importance to the Grouping): **Essential** =
  Everyday, Health, Home, Transportation, Income Taxes; **Priorities** = Banking
  & Investing, Debt, Fitness, Kids, Rental; **Other** = Discretionary, Gifts,
  Travel. Where the source spreadsheet split a Grouping across importances (e.g.
  Home's Garden/Household goods were "Other"), it now rolls up under the
  Grouping's single Importance. Change with a one-row `UPDATE` on
  `category_groups.importance_area_id`.
- **Aggregation** `src/lib/utils/spendingReport.ts` — the pure
  `buildSpendingReport(expenses, categories, groups, importanceAreas, year)`.
  21 unit tests in `spendingReport.spec.ts` (month columns, roll-up/subtotals,
  ordering, Uncategorized, refund netting, FX, null amounts, blank-vs-zero cells).
  Per-cell `{ amount, count }` drives blank (count 0) vs `0.00` (net-zero but had
  activity).
- **Types** `src/lib/types/Hierarchy.ts` (`ImportanceArea`, `CategoryGroup`);
  `Category` gains `group_id`.
- **Service** `CategoryService` gains `getFamilyImportanceAreas`,
  `getFamilyGroups`, and `createDefaultHierarchy` (RPC wrapper).
- **Page + nav** `src/routes/spending/+page.svelte` + a **Spending** top-level
  tab. Self-seeds the hierarchy on first open (mirrors default-categories
  lazy-init), then loads hierarchy + the year's expenses and paints the grid.
  Year prev/next selector, missing-amount footnote, Importance bands, Grouping
  and Importance subtotals, Uncategorized section, Grand Total.
- **Rendering details.** Long category names truncate to one line
  (`max-w-64 truncate`) with the full name on hover via `title`. The layout gives
  `/spending` full window width (`max-w-full`); other pages keep `max-w-5xl`.

full unit suite green (1278 passed / 8 skipped, incl. the 21 new). Production
build succeeds. Not yet exercised: a rendered end-to-end pass (no local
auth/seed harness) — validated live by the maintainer instead.

or renamed category lands in Uncategorized until its `group_id` is set by hand.
